lines.text: Keep a steady pace. A squad that sprints the first hour walks the rest.
Eyes on the treeline, not your feet. The road will still be there.
Count the milestones. If we're lost, I want to know how lost.
Talk if you like, but quietly. Voices carry further out here.
We'll rest at the next stream. Fill your canteens there, not before.
Are we nearly there? Don't laugh, I'm only asking once.
I've never been this far from the village. The trees even smell different.
Race you to that big rock? No? Fine. Later.
I packed six rice balls. Six. Want one?
Does the road look like the map to you? Because it doesn't to me.
That hill there? My grandfather farmed it before the road was paved.
You ninja walk so quietly. It's unnerving, honestly.
I make this trip every season. Never with company before.
There's a tea house at the crossroads. Best roasted chestnuts this side of the river.
Do they teach you to carry that much without complaining? I'm impressed.
Watches in pairs, two hours each. Wake the next pair, don't just nudge them.
Small fire, low smoke. We're guests in these woods.
Eat, then sleep. Tomorrow's a long road.
Good work today. I mean that. Now get some rest.
Sit a while. Tell me something you learned today that the Academy didn't teach you.
Can you see all those stars? There's never this many over the village.
I can't sleep. Want to talk for a bit?
Do you think we're doing well? On this mission, I mean.
If you snore, I'm putting a leaf in your mouth.
This is the first time I've slept outside. It's not so bad, with the squad here.
Thank you for the fire. And the company. I don't usually have either on the road.
I brought dried persimmons. Here, take a handful. Go on.
My family thinks I'm mad, travelling with goods at my age. Maybe I am.
You lot sleep in shifts? Then I'll sleep soundly. First time in years.
Tell me about the Leaf. I only ever see the market.
We're here. Stay together and let me do the talking.
Good. On time and in one piece. That's a mission done right.
Look around. Remember this place. You'll be back one day.
Rest tonight. We report in the morning.
Well done, all of you. That road was longer than it looked.
We made it! We really made it!
It's so different from home! Look at the roofs!
Can we get something to eat first? Please?
I'm writing this down. First town I've ever been to.
My legs have turned to jelly. Worth it, though.
Here we are. I'd thought the trip would be worse. Much worse.
My shop's just past the well. Come in, have some tea before you go.
I'll be telling everyone the Leaf's ninja are the best on the road.
Thank you for seeing me home. Truly.
Ha! Not one bandit. You must have frightened them off just by walking.
Down! Protect the client!
Ambush. Positions, now. Nobody chases them into the trees.
Stay calm. Remember your drills. Guard the cart.
Form up behind me. Watch the sides, not just the front.
They want the goods, not a fight. Let's make sure they get neither.
They're in the trees! Everyone, look out!
I'll cover the client! Go!
Bandits! Real ones! Okay. Okay. I can do this.
Back to back! Like we practised!
I knew that bird call sounded wrong!
Bandits! I knew it! I knew it!
Not the cart! Please, not the cart!
Do something! That's what I'm paying you for!
I'll stay under the wagon, if that's all right with everyone.
Oh, spare me! I'm only a poor merchant!
Good. Check for injuries, then check the cart.
That's how it's done. Calm, together, no one left behind.
You did well. All of you. I'll say so in the report.
Tie them and leave them for the border patrol. We keep moving.
Breathe. It's over. Drink some water.
We won! Did you see me? Did you see?
My hands won't stop shaking. Is that normal?
Good teamwork! Really good. High five!
We did it without anyone getting hurt. That's the best part.
I'm starving now. Fighting makes you hungry.
Remarkable! I've never seen anything like it!
You're worth every ryo. Every single one.
My heart's still pounding. Thank you, thank you.
I'll be adding a bonus to your pay. Don't argue.
And you're just Genin? Imagine the Jonin!
C-rank, escort. {client} travels to {place} and wants a squad alongside. Two days' walk. {pay}.
Escort duty for {client}, as far as {place}. Bandits have been seen on that road. Stay sharp. {pay}.
Your squad's first escort? {client} to {place}, door to door. Keep the client comfortable and alive to complain. {pay}.
I'm bound for {place} with my wares. I've heard stories about that road. I'd like some ninja with me.
You're my escort? You look young. No offence. The last escort was all beard and no sense.
Just see me to {place} in one piece. And my cart. Mostly my cart.
Good. We leave at dawn from the main gate. Don't be late.
Excellent. I walk slowly and complain often. You've been warned.
Right then. I'll pack an extra rice ball for each of you.
No? I'll wait for another squad. I'm not walking that road alone.
Pity. I'll hire someone from the next village, if I live that long.
Hm. Fine. The Mission Desk will find me someone braver.
How much further? My feet are writing letters of complaint.
Did you hear that? In the trees? No? Just a bird? Good.
We've made good time. At this pace, {place} by tomorrow evening.
{place}! At last! I owe you a fine meal, all of you.
Not a scratch on me or the cart. You're welcome to escort me any time.
We're here. I didn't think we'd make it so smoothly. Tell the Leaf I said so.
I'll walk the rest myself. You've been more trouble than the road.
My cart's in a ditch and my wares are in a river. Some escort.
We turned back? After all that? I'll want words with your Mission Desk.
Escort to {place}, complete. {client} wrote a letter. A long letter. Mostly good.
Logged. Your first road out of the village and back. How was it?
Good work. Escorts are the backbone of C-rank. Quiet, long, and worth every ryo.
C-rank. {count} bandits are holding the road near {place}. {client} wants them gone. Drive them off or bring them in. {pay}.
Bandit trouble at {place}. Thieves, not shinobi, as far as we know. {count} of them. Careful anyway. {pay}.
{client} has lost three carts this month near {place}. Clear the bandits, bring back what you can. {pay}.
They come out of the trees at {place}. {count}, maybe more. They took my whole harvest.
We can't take our goods to market. Nobody can. Not with those bandits on the road.
I'm not asking you to hurt them. Just make them leave. And maybe bring back my rice.
Thank you. The bend by the twin pines is where they hide.
Bring back what you can. Even half the rice would carry us through winter.
Good. Be careful. They're cowards, but cowards in a crowd are bold.
Then the road stays closed, and the market goes hungry.
I see. I'll ask the Desk to post it again.
No one wants to face them. I don't blame you, but I hoped.
Did you find their camp? Are they still there?
They say one of them has a club the size of a log. Mind that one.
Fewer on the road this week. Something's working.
The road's open! We'll be at market by the weekend!
You brought back my rice! And my cart! And... my neighbour's goat?
No more bandits. I'll sleep tonight for the first time in a month.
They're still out there. Worse, they're angry now.
You let them go? All of them? With my rice?
The road's no safer than it was. I'll wait for a stronger squad.
Bandits cleared from {place}. Those you brought in are with the police. Well done.
Logged. {client} sent a sack of rice to the Desk. We're keeping it.
Good. Remember this one: you won without hurting more than you had to. That's the job.
Long-distance delivery: {item} to {target}, all the way to {place}. Four days there and back. {pay}.
C-rank courier work. {client} needs {item} in {target}'s hands at {place}. Sealed. Don't open it. {pay}.
A far run for {client}: {place}, past the river crossing. The parcel is {item}. Pack for rain. {pay}.
This {item} has to reach {target} in {place}. It can't go with the merchants. Too many hands.
I'd go myself, but my knees and that road don't get along. Please, {place}, and quickly.
Give it to {target} and no one else. If {target} isn't there, bring it home.
Good. Here. Keep it dry and keep it close.
Thank you. {target} will know it's from me by the knot.
Safe travels. And bring back news of {place}, if you can.
It's a long way, I know. I'll find someone.
Then it waits. Some things are worth waiting for.
No? Hm. The Desk will have another squad soon.
Is it still sealed? Good. Good.
How far to {place} now? Two more days, maybe less.
Rest at the inn by the ford. They know the Leaf there.
All the way from the Leaf? For me? Thank {client} for me. Thank you, too.
It's here, and it's sealed. You've no idea what this means.
{target} has it. I can stop worrying now. Thank you.
It's opened. The seal's broken. This is no use to anyone now.
You lost it? On the road? Where on the road?
Too late. {target} left {place} two days ago.
Delivery to {place}, confirmed. A thank-you letter came back by hawk this morning.
Logged. Long road, that one. You've earned a bath and a hot meal.
Good. Courier work across the border is how the Leaf keeps its friends. Remember that.
D-rank, lost pet. {client} hasn't seen {target} since yesterday. Last sighting near {place}. Pays {pay}.
A pet search for {client}. The animal answers to {target}, apparently. Try {place} first. {pay} on return.
{client} is offering {pay} for {target}, safe and sound. Bring a treat and patience. Mostly patience.
You're the one from the Mission Desk? Thank goodness. {target} slipped out the back gate and never came home.
{target} always goes to {place} when there's a storm coming. Please, I've looked everywhere else.
It's {target}. My {target}. Small, scruffy, bites when frightened. Don't take it personally.
You'll really look? Here, take this. It's {target}'s favourite dried fish.
Thank you. Call the name softly, it hates shouting.
Bless you. I'll leave the gate open and the bowl full.
Oh. Of course. You must be busy with real missions.
Never mind. I'll keep walking the streets myself.
I understand. If you see {target} anyway, just... tell me?
Any sign? Even a paw print?
Someone saw something small and scruffy by {place}. Could be.
Don't grab at it. Crouch down and let it come to you.
{target}! You're home! Look at you, all burrs and mud!
You found {target}! I could cry. I might cry. Thank you.
There's my troublemaker. Thank you, truly. Go and claim your pay.
Look, it remembers me! Thank you for bringing {target} back.
Still nothing? I suppose that's it, then.
Maybe {target} found a new home. I hope it's a kind one.
Thank you for trying. Really. It's not your fault.
Pet returned. {client} sent a note. Most of it is just the word "thank you".
Another lost animal home. Logged. Wash your hands, would you?
Done, then. You'd be amazed how many of these we get. Pay's at the counter.
Weeding at {place}. {count} rows, by hand. {client} is paying {pay}. Bring gloves.
D-rank for {client}: clear the weeds from {place} before they choke the beans. {pay}.
Garden work at {place}. Not glamorous, but every Genin does it. {pay}.
The weeds have taken {place} over. {count} beds of them. My back won't let me bend any more.
Pull them up by the root, mind, or they're back in a week. All {count} rows.
Not the little purple ones! Those are herbs. Everything else goes.
Wonderful. The basket's by the shed. Fill it as many times as you need.
Good. Start at the far end, by the fence. It's worst there.
Thank you. I'll bring you barley tea at noon.
Fine. The weeds and I will keep arguing on our own.
No one wants the weeding. I know. I know.
Pity. My knees were counting on you.
That's the way. Get the roots, not just the tops.
You're faster than the last Genin. Much less complaining, too.
Half done already? Have a drink. It's hot work.
Look at that! I can see the soil again!
Every row clear. My vegetables thank you, and so do I.
Lovely work. Not a dandelion left standing.
You pulled up the radishes. All of them. Every single one.
Half the beds are still green. I'll finish myself, I suppose.
That's not weeding, that's just stepping on things.
Weeding done. {client} says you can come back any spring.
Logged. There's dirt on the report form. There's always dirt on these.
Good. Garden missions build patience. Your sensei will tell you the same.
Delivery. {client} needs {item} taken to {target} at {place}. Don't drop it. {pay}.
Simple run: {item}, from {client} to {target}. {place}. Back by evening. {pay}.
D-rank courier work. {item} for {target}. {client} says it's fragile, so it's fragile.
This {item} has to reach {target} at {place} today. It can't wait.
Take it straight there, no detours, and put it in {target}'s hands. Nobody else's.
It's {item}. Careful, it's heavier than it looks. {target} at {place} is expecting it.
Perfect. Here. Hold it with both hands.
Thank you. Tell {target} I said hello.
Good. Off you go, and don't run on the bridge with it.
No? I'll ask the courier, then. Slower, but they'll go.
Ah. I suppose I'll carry it myself, slowly.
All right. Someone else will take it.
Not delivered yet? {target} will be wondering.
You still have it? Good. Keep it out of the rain.
{place} is that way, past the noodle stand. You can't miss it.
Ah, the {item}! Right on time. {client} always sends the good ones.
Delivered and in one piece. Thank you. Tell {client} it arrived.
That's mine? Wonderful. Here, I'll sign for it.
It's broken. You brought me a broken {item}.
Too late. The day I needed it has come and gone.
That's not even mine. Did you mix up the parcels?
Delivery confirmed. {target} signed for it. Good, clear handwriting for once.
Logged. Three more of these on the board, if your legs are up for it.
Done. Most of the village's post goes through Genin, you know. Not much glory, plenty of trust.
Babysitting for {client}. {count} hours with {target}. Bring a book. Bring two. {pay}.
{client} has an errand across the village. Watch {target} till they're back. {pay}.
Childminding, D-rank. {target} is, I'm told, "a bit lively". Read that how you like. {pay}.
I'll only be {count} hours. {target} is no trouble. Mostly no trouble.
Bedtime is after supper. No sweets. Fine, one sweet. One!
{target} has been begging to meet a real ninja. Please don't do anything too exciting.
Thank you! Snacks are on the shelf. The high one.
Oh, you're a lifesaver. Don't let {target} near the paints.
Good. If anything happens, the neighbour across the way knows what to do.
Oh dear. I'll have to take {target} with me, then.
I don't blame you. I'd run too.
No? That's all right. Grandma can probably manage. Probably.
Is everything all right? It's very quiet. Quiet is suspicious.
You've lasted an hour! That's a record.
Did {target} eat anything that wasn't food? Just checking.
You're both still smiling! What's your secret?
{target} says you're the best ninja in the whole village. High praise.
The house is standing and everyone's fed. Thank you, really.
Why is the cat painted blue?
{target} is on the roof. How is {target} on the roof?
I came home to tears. Everyone's, by the look of it.
Babysitting complete. You look more tired than after a C-rank. They always do.
{client} has already asked for you again. That's a compliment, or a warning.
Logged. Sit down a moment before the next one. Children are harder than bandits.
Repairs at {place}. {client}'s {item} needs fixing before the next rain. {pay}.
D-rank handiwork for {client}: {count} boards on the {item} at {place}. Tools provided. {pay}.
{client} needs help mending the {item}. Hammer, nails, honest work. {pay}.
The storm took half the {item}. I've got the wood, I just haven't got the hands.
{count} boards, all rotten through. Pull them, replace them, done. Easy for a ninja.
Mind the old nails. Some of them have been in that {item} longer than I've been alive.
Good. Hammer's in the bucket. Watch your thumbs.
Thank you. Start with the corner; it leans worst.
Fine, fine. Measure twice before you cut, mind.
Then the {item} can fall down a bit more. It's good at that.
I'll ask a Kinoshita carpenter. Expensive, but they'll come.
All right. I'll prop it with a broom and hope.
Straight! Keep it straight! Look along the edge.
That's sounding good. Steady knocks, not angry ones.
How many left? Don't skip any, I'll be counting.
Look at that. Sturdier than it was new.
It doesn't wobble! It's never not wobbled!
Fine work. You could do this for a living, if the ninja business ever dries up.
It's crooked. It's very crooked. It's worse than before.
You nailed the door shut. From the outside.
I'll have to call a carpenter to fix your fixing.
Repair done, {client} says. Also says you hammer like a woodpecker. Fondly, I think.
Logged. Half the village's fences have a Genin's nails in them somewhere.
Good. The Kinoshita carpenters will grumble you're taking their work. Ignore them.
